q: The Pension Payment Order issued in favour of a retired railway servant is prepared and issued in the manner that:

options.A: It is issued in two halves, one half being retained by the pension disbursing authority and the other half being given to the pensioner
options.B: A single copy is issued, which remains with the Accounts Office alone
options.C: It is issued only to the treasury, and no part of it is given to the pensioner
options.D: It is issued afresh every year to the pensioner by the disbursing bank

e: A Pension Payment Order is issued in two halves, the disbursing authority half and the pensioner half, so that payment can be identified and verified by both.

q: A candidate selected for appointment to a railway post is allowed to join duty, his verification of character and antecedents not yet having been completed. In regard to the nature of his appointment in such a case, the correct position is that:

options.A: The appointment is regular and final from the date of his joining in all respects
options.B: The appointment is provisional, subject to the verification of his character and antecedents, and is liable to be terminated if the verification report is found to be adverse
options.C: Verification of character and antecedents is not required for any railway appointment
options.D: The appointment becomes final automatically on the expiry of one month from joining

e: Appointment made before completion of verification of character and antecedents is provisional and liable to termination if the verification report is adverse.

q: A railway servant on tour is required to halt continuously at an outstation on duty for a very long period, extending beyond 180 days at a stretch. In regard to the treatment of such a continuous halt for the purpose of Travelling Allowance, the correct position is that:

options.A: Daily Allowance continues to be admissible at full rates for the entire halt, however long it may be
options.B: No Daily Allowance at all is admissible for any halt on tour
options.C: A continuous halt on tour extending beyond 180 days is treated as a transfer for the purpose of Travelling Allowance
options.D: The halt is treated as leave for the period beyond 30 days

e: For Travelling Allowance, a continuous halt on tour beyond 180 days is treated as a transfer, so full Daily Allowance does not continue indefinitely.

q: A railway servant has made a valid nomination for the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity payable on his death and, while still in service, wishes to change the nomination in favour of another member of his family. In regard to such a change, the correct position is that:

options.A: A nomination once made can never be changed under any circumstances
options.B: A nomination can be changed only after the retirement of the railway servant
options.C: A nomination can be changed only with the permission of a court of law
options.D: He may modify or cancel the nomination at any time before his retirement by giving a notice in writing in the prescribed manner, whereupon the earlier nomination stands modified or cancelled accordingly

e: A gratuity nomination may be modified or cancelled at any time before retirement by written notice in the prescribed manner, and the earlier nomination then stands modified or cancelled.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for 8 hours on a day, and the admissible rate of Daily Allowance for the station is Rs 900 per day. Daily Allowance for an absence of more than 6 hours but not exceeding 12 hours being admissible at 70 per cent of the rate, the amount admissible to him for that day will be:

options.A: Rs 630
options.B: Rs 900
options.C: Rs 450
options.D: Rs 270

e: Daily Allowance for absence over 6 hours but not over 12 hours is 70 per cent of the rate; 70 per cent of Rs 900 = Rs 630.

q: A railway servant availed Extra Ordinary Leave for 40 days during a half-year. The Leave on Average Pay to be credited in advance to his leave account at the beginning of the succeeding half-year, after reduction at the rate of one-tenth of the period of such leave, will be:

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 11 days
options.C: 13 days
options.D: 9 days

e: Advance Leave on Average Pay credit is reduced by one-tenth of Extra Ordinary Leave availed: 40 / 10 = 4 days, so 15 - 4 = 11 days.

q: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, the fee prescribed for obtaining a copy of information in A-4 or A-3 size paper is charged at the rate of:

options.A: Rs 5 per page
options.B: Rs 10 per page
options.C: Rs 2 per page
options.D: Rs 50 per page

e: The RTI (Fee and Cost) Rules prescribe Rs 2 per page for a copy of information on A-4 or A-3 size paper.

q: Under Section 19 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the bonus payable to an employee for an accounting year shall ordinarily be paid by the employer within a period of:

options.A: 8 months from the close of the accounting year
options.B: 1 month from the close of the accounting year
options.C: 3 months from the close of the accounting year
options.D: 12 months from the close of the accounting year

e: Section 19 of the Payment of Bonus Act requires bonus for an accounting year to be paid within eight months from the close of that accounting year.

q: A railway servant acquires a lien on a post in the manner that he:

options.A: Acquires it from the very first day of his probation on that post
options.B: Acquires it only after he has put in ten years of service in the cadre
options.C: Acquires it automatically on the expiry of two years from his appointment, whether confirmed or not
options.D: Holds it on the permanent post to which he is confirmed (appointed substantively), a probationer having no lien on the post

e: Lien is held on the permanent post to which a servant is appointed substantively, that is confirmed; a probationer has no lien on the post.

q: Commuted leave granted to a railway servant on medical certificate is subject to the condition that:

options.A: It can be granted to a railway servant only once in his entire service
options.B: The authority sanctioning it should have reason to believe that the railway servant will return to duty on the expiry of the leave
options.C: It can be granted only to gazetted railway servants
options.D: It must be followed immediately by retirement of the railway servant

e: Commuted leave on medical certificate can be granted only if the sanctioning authority has reason to believe the servant will return to duty on expiry of the leave.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 180 days of Leave on Average Pay and 150 days of Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit. His pay plus Dearness Allowance at retirement is Rs 1,20,000 per month. The total cash equivalent of leave salary admissible to him on retirement, the shortfall in Leave on Average Pay being made good from Leave on Half Average Pay at half rate so that the total does not exceed 300 days, will be:
e: Encashment: 180 days LAP at Rs 1,20,000 / 30 = Rs 7,20,000, plus 120 days from LHAP at half rate Rs 60,000 / 30 x 120 = Rs 2,40,000, total Rs 9,60,000 for 300 days.

q: Under Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, in an establishment in which less than one thousand persons are employed, the wages of an employed person shall be paid before the expiry of:

options.A: The seventh day after the last day of the wage period
options.B: The tenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.C: The fifteenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.D: The last day of the wage period itself

e: Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act requires wages in an establishment employing less than one thousand persons to be paid before expiry of the seventh day after the wage period.

q: A railway servant habitually reports late for duty and repeatedly fails to complete the work allotted to him within the time fixed for it. Under Rule 3 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, such habitual conduct on his part amounts to:

options.A: No lapse at all, as it is a purely administrative matter
options.B: A lapse punishable only under the Factories Act, 1948
options.C: Grounds only for transfer to another office
options.D: A lack of devotion to duty on the part of the railway servant

e: Rule 3 of the Conduct Rules requires devotion to duty; habitual late attendance and failure to complete work in time amount to lack of devotion to duty.

q: Recovery of a House Building Advance granted to a railway servant is effected from his pay in the manner that:

options.A: The principal and the interest are recovered together in not more than 100 monthly instalments
options.B: The principal is recovered first in not more than 180 monthly instalments and the interest thereafter in not more than 60 monthly instalments
options.C: The interest is recovered first in 60 monthly instalments and the principal thereafter in 180 monthly instalments
options.D: The whole amount, principal and interest, is recovered in a single instalment at the time of retirement

e: House Building Advance principal is recovered first in not more than 180 monthly instalments and interest thereafter in not more than 60 monthly instalments.

q: The minimum family pension admissible to the family of a deceased railway servant under the 7th CPC dispensation, exclusive of Dearness Relief, is:

options.A: Rs 3,500 per month
options.B: Rs 7,850 per month
options.C: Rs 9,000 per month
options.D: Rs 12,500 per month

e: The minimum family pension under the 7th CPC is Rs 9,000 per month, exclusive of Dearness Relief.

q: Under Section 49 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a Welfare Officer is required to be appointed in every factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is:

options.A: Five hundred or more
options.B: One hundred or more
options.C: Two hundred and fifty or more
options.D: One thousand or more

e: Section 49 of the Factories Act requires a Welfare Officer in every factory where five hundred or more workers are ordinarily employed.

q: A subscriber to the National Pension System dies while in service, before superannuation. In regard to the accumulated pension wealth standing in his Tier-I account, the correct position is that:

options.A: The entire amount is forfeited to the Government
options.B: Only the subscriber's own contribution is paid to the nominee, the Government contribution being forfeited
options.C: The nominee must compulsorily purchase an annuity with the entire amount
options.D: The nominee or legal heir is entitled to withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth as a lump sum

e: On death in service of an NPS subscriber, the nominee or legal heir may withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth in the Tier-I account as a lump sum.

q: The leave salary payable to a male railway servant during a spell of paternity leave admissible to him is equal to:

options.A: Half of the pay last drawn by him before proceeding on leave
options.B: The pay last drawn by him before proceeding on leave
options.C: The leave salary admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay
options.D: Nil, as paternity leave carries no leave salary

e: Paternity leave salary equals the pay last drawn by the male railway servant immediately before proceeding on such leave.

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner is Rs 42,000 per month. On his attaining the age of 100 years, the additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 100 per cent of his basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 21,000 per month
options.B: Rs 33,600 per month
options.C: Rs 42,000 per month
options.D: Rs 12,600 per month

e: Additional pension at age 100 is 100 per cent of basic pension; 100 per cent of Rs 42,000 = Rs 42,000 per month.

q: The employment of a worker in a railway workshop, governed by the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, is terminated by or on behalf of the employer in the middle of a wage period. The wages earned by him and payable to him for that wage period shall be paid:

options.A: Before the expiry of the second working day from the day on which his employment is terminated
options.B: Before the expiry of the seventh day from the day on which his employment is terminated
options.C: Along with the wages of the other staff for that wage period, in the usual course
options.D: Only after the expiry of one month from the day on which his employment is terminated

e: Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act requires wages of a terminated employee to be paid before expiry of the second working day from the date of termination.

q: A Central Public Information Officer of the Railways fails to furnish the information sought by an applicant within the time specified under the Right to Information Act, 2005, and furnishes it after the expiry of that time. In such a case, the information is required to be furnished:

options.A: On payment of double the normal fee
options.B: Only after obtaining the orders of the Central Information Commission
options.C: On payment of a penalty fee of Rs 250 per day of delay
options.D: Free of charge to the applicant

e: If information is not furnished within the time specified under the RTI Act, Section 7 requires it to be furnished free of charge thereafter.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 40,000 per month applies for a House Building Advance. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him, at 139 times his basic pay and within the overall ceiling of Rs 1 crore, will be:
e: House Building Advance maximum is 139 times basic pay, subject to the Rs 1 crore ceiling; 139 x Rs 40,000 = Rs 55,60,000.

q: A railway servant who is under suspension applies for the grant of leave to him for a period falling within the period of his suspension. The correct action on his application is that:

options.A: Leave on Average Pay at his credit may be granted to him as usual
options.B: Only casual leave may be granted to him during suspension
options.C: No leave of any kind can be granted to a railway servant under suspension
options.D: Extra Ordinary Leave may be granted to him without any restriction

e: No leave of any kind can be granted to a railway servant under suspension for a period falling within the suspension period.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, an 'employee' for the purpose of eligibility for bonus under the Act is a person employed on a salary or wage not exceeding:

options.A: Rs 21,000 per month
options.B: Rs 10,000 per month
options.C: Rs 15,000 per month
options.D: Rs 25,000 per month

e: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, an employee drawing salary or wage not exceeding Rs 21,000 per month is eligible for bonus under the Act.

q: A railway servant avails Leave Travel Concession for himself, while the members of his family travel to the same destination separately, on different dates, without accompanying him. In regard to the Leave Travel Concession claim of the family members, the correct position is that:

options.A: The claim is not admissible, as the family must travel along with the railway servant
options.B: The claim is admissible only if the family travels on the same train as the railway servant
options.C: The claim is admissible only for the journey performed after the railway servant returns
options.D: The claim is admissible, as the family members may avail the concession independently of the railway servant

e: Family members may avail Leave Travel Concession independently of the railway servant, travelling separately to the same destination on different dates.

q: A railway pensioner surrenders Rs 2,500 per month of his pension for commutation. The commutation value expressed as number of years' purchase for his age on the next birthday is 8.371. The lump sum amount payable to him on commutation will be:
e: Commuted value is Rs 2,500 x 8.371 x 12 = Rs 2,51,130, using the years purchase factor for the age on the next birthday.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, an adolescent who has completed fifteen years of age but has not completed eighteen years shall not be required or allowed to work in a factory unless:

options.A: He has completed the prescribed course of training in the factory
options.B: A certificate of fitness granted to him by a certifying surgeon is in the custody of the manager of the factory and he carries a token giving a reference to that certificate while at work
options.C: He has obtained the written permission of his parent or guardian
options.D: He is employed only on work of a clerical nature

e: Section 68 of the Factories Act bars an adolescent from working unless a certifying surgeon fitness certificate is in the manager custody and he carries a token referring to it.

q: Departmental proceedings are proposed to be instituted against a retired railway servant, in respect of a grave misconduct committed by him while in service, the proceedings not having been instituted before his retirement. Such proceedings can be instituted only:

options.A: By the disciplinary authority which was competent to punish him while in service, without any other sanction
options.B: Within ten years of the event, with the sanction of the Railway Board
options.C: With the sanction of the President, and not in respect of any event which took place more than four years before the institution of the proceedings
options.D: At any time after retirement, without any limitation as to the period of the event

e: Departmental proceedings against a retired servant for an event over four years old, or not instituted before retirement, require the sanction of the President under the Pension Rules.

q: In regard to the entry of the date of birth of a railway servant in his Service Book at the time of his appointment, the prescribed practice is that the date of birth is:

options.A: Recorded in figures only, on the basis of the school leaving certificate
options.B: Left to be recorded after the completion of his probation
options.C: Recorded on the oral declaration of the railway servant, without any documentary proof
options.D: Recorded both in words and in figures and attested by the Head of Office

e: Date of birth in the Service Book is recorded both in words and in figures at appointment and attested by the Head of Office.

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 68,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, being 50 per cent of the last pay drawn, for the period for which that rate is admissible, will be:

options.A: Rs 20,400 per month
options.B: Rs 34,000 per month
options.C: Rs 27,200 per month
options.D: Rs 40,800 per month

e: Enhanced family pension is 50 per cent of last pay drawn; 50 per cent of Rs 68,000 = Rs 34,000 per month.

q: From the wages payable to a railway servant employed in a workshop, governed by the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, deductions can lawfully be made:

options.A: Only for the heads authorised under the Act, such as fines, absence from duty, damage or loss, house accommodation, recovery of advances and income tax
options.B: For any purpose which the employer considers proper
options.C: Only towards recovery of advances taken by the railway servant
options.D: Only towards income tax and provident fund subscription

e: Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act permits deductions only for authorised heads such as fines, absence, damage or loss, house accommodation, advances and income tax.

q: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the monthly subscription payable by a Group 'C' railway servant, in respect of the insurance cover and savings admissible to his group, is:

options.A: Rs 120 per month
options.B: Rs 60 per month
options.C: Rs 30 per month
options.D: Rs 15 per month

e: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the monthly subscription for Group C staff is Rs 30 per month.

q: A railway servant seeks voluntary retirement after completing the prescribed qualifying service and gives the required notice of three months. He requests that a shorter notice may be accepted in his case. The correct position is that:

options.A: The notice period can on no account be shortened
options.B: A shorter notice can be accepted only by the Railway Board
options.C: The notice period is automatically reduced to one month on the request of the railway servant
options.D: The appointing authority may, in special circumstances, relax the requirement of the notice period and accept a shorter notice

e: The appointing authority may, in special circumstances, relax the three months notice requirement for voluntary retirement and accept a shorter notice.

q: An adult worker employed in a railway workshop, governed by the Factories Act, 1948, has worked for 240 days in the preceding calendar year. The leave with wages earned by him for the succeeding year, at one day for every twenty days of work performed, will be:

options.A: 20 days
options.B: 12 days
options.C: 24 days
options.D: 10 days

e: Leave with wages under the Factories Act is one day per 20 days worked; 240 / 20 = 12 days for the succeeding year.

q: Under Rule 14 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to public demonstrations in honour of a railway servant, no railway servant shall, except with the previous sanction of the competent authority:

options.A: Receive any complimentary address or accept any testimonial, or attend any meeting or entertainment held in his honour or in the honour of any other railway servant
options.B: Attend the marriage ceremony of a fellow railway servant
options.C: Accept an invitation to a public function in his personal capacity
options.D: Be felicitated by the members of his own family at his residence

e: Rule 14 of the Conduct Rules bars a railway servant, without previous sanction, from receiving a complimentary address or testimonial or attending a meeting or entertainment in his honour.

q: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the maximum amount of gratuity payable to an employee, as revised with effect from 29th March, 2018, is:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 16 lakh
options.C: Rs 20 lakh
options.D: Rs 25 lakh

e: The maximum gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act was raised to Rs 20 lakh with effect from 29th March 2018.

q: A railway servant under suspension is reinstated in service after the proceedings against him end in his honourable exoneration. In regard to his pay and allowances for the period of suspension and the treatment of that period, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is entitled only to the subsistence allowance already paid to him, and the period is treated as leave without pay
options.B: He is entitled to half of the pay and allowances for the period of suspension
options.C: The period of suspension is treated as a break in his service for all purposes
options.D: He is entitled to the full pay and allowances to which he would have been entitled had he not been suspended, less the subsistence allowance already paid, and the period is treated as a period spent on duty

e: On honourable exoneration and reinstatement, the servant gets full pay and allowances less subsistence allowance already paid, and the suspension period is treated as duty.

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme draws basic pay of Rs 50,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 30,000 per month. The total contribution payable by the Government in his case, at 18.5 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance towards the individual corpus and the pool corpus together, will be:

options.A: Rs 8,000 per month
options.B: Rs 14,800 per month
options.C: Rs 10,000 per month
options.D: Rs 18,500 per month

e: Government contribution under UPS is 18.5 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance; 18.5 per cent of Rs 80,000 = Rs 14,800 per month.

q: Under the Railway Pension Rules, the expression 'pension', as defined therein, is to be understood in the manner that:

options.A: Pension includes gratuity, except when the term pension is used in contradistinction to gratuity
options.B: Pension never includes gratuity in any context
options.C: Pension includes only the monthly payment and the commuted value thereof
options.D: Pension and gratuity are one and the same benefit for all purposes

e: Under the Railway Pension Rules, pension includes gratuity except when the term pension is used in contradistinction to gratuity.

q: In regard to leave admissible to a person engaged as an apprentice under the Apprentices Act, 1961, in a railway establishment, the correct position is that he is entitled, during a year of his apprenticeship, to:

options.A: Leave on Average Pay of 30 days, as admissible to a regular railway servant
options.B: No leave of any kind during the period of apprenticeship
options.C: Casual leave of 12 days, besides medical leave and extraordinary leave as admissible under the Apprentices Rules
options.D: Only unpaid leave, at the discretion of his immediate supervisor

e: An apprentice under the Apprentices Act is entitled to casual leave of 12 days in a year, besides medical and extraordinary leave as per the Apprentices Rules.

q: A railway servant tenders his resignation from railway service and, before the resignation is accepted and becomes effective, seeks to withdraw it. In regard to such withdrawal, the correct position is that:

options.A: A resignation, once tendered, can never be withdrawn in any circumstances
options.B: The resignation can be withdrawn only after the railway servant rejoins duty
options.C: The withdrawal is automatic and does not require the approval of any authority
options.D: The railway servant may be permitted by the competent authority to withdraw his resignation before it becomes effective

e: A resignation may be withdrawn, with permission of the competent authority, before it is accepted and becomes effective.

q: Under Section 80 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a worker who is granted leave with wages is paid, for the period of his leave, at a rate equal to:

options.A: Half of his average daily earnings
options.B: The daily average of his total full-time earnings for the days on which he actually worked during the month immediately preceding his leave
options.C: A flat rate fixed by the manager of the factory
options.D: His earnings of the last day worked before proceeding on leave

e: Section 80 of the Factories Act pays leave wages at the daily average of total full-time earnings for days actually worked in the month immediately preceding the leave.

q: In direct recruitment to posts on the Railways, the reservation admissible for ex-servicemen in non-gazetted Group 'C' posts is:

options.A: 10 per cent of the vacancies
options.B: 20 per cent of the vacancies
options.C: 5 per cent of the vacancies
options.D: 15 per cent of the vacancies

e: Reservation for ex-servicemen in direct recruitment to non-gazetted Group C posts on the Railways is 10 per cent of the vacancies.

q: A railway pensioner has commuted a portion of his pension for a lump sum payment. In regard to the Dearness Relief admissible to him on his pension, the correct position is that Dearness Relief is calculated:

options.A: Only on the reduced pension actually drawn by him after commutation
options.B: Only on the commuted lump sum amount paid to him
options.C: On the original basic pension, that is, the pension before the deduction of the commuted portion
options.D: At half the normal rate, so long as any portion of his pension stands commuted

e: Dearness Relief is calculated on the original basic pension before commutation, not on the reduced pension drawn after commutation.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in regard to the employment of a child as a domestic help by a railway servant, the correct position is that no railway servant shall:

options.A: Employ any domestic help at his residence
options.B: Employ a person above the age of eighteen years as domestic help without sanction
options.C: Employ a domestic help who is a relative of another railway servant
options.D: Employ any child below the age of fourteen years as a domestic servant or for any other work at his residence

e: The Conduct Rules prohibit a railway servant from employing any child below fourteen years as a domestic servant or for any other work at his residence.

q: Under Section 8 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, the total amount of fine that can be imposed on an employed person in respect of a wage period shall not exceed:

options.A: 10 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period
options.B: 3 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period
options.C: 25 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period
options.D: 50 per cent of the wages payable to him for that wage period

e: Section 8 of the Payment of Wages Act caps the total fine in a wage period at 3 per cent of the wages payable for that period.

q: A railway servant retires from service while in occupation of a railway quarter, and an amount is found outstanding against him on account of licence fee for the period of his occupation of the quarter. In regard to the recovery of that amount, the correct position is that:

options.A: The outstanding licence fee can be recovered from the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity admissible to him
options.B: The outstanding amount is automatically written off on his retirement
options.C: The amount can be recovered only through a civil suit against the retired railway servant
options.D: The amount can be recovered only from the monthly pension payable to him, by attachment

e: Outstanding licence fee for a railway quarter can be recovered from the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity admissible to the retiring railway servant.

q: Under Section 45 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, first-aid boxes or cupboards, equipped with the prescribed contents, are required to be provided and maintained in a factory at the rate of:

options.A: One for every 50 workers ordinarily employed
options.B: One for every 500 workers ordinarily employed
options.C: One for every 150 workers ordinarily employed
options.D: One for every 300 workers ordinarily employed

e: Section 45 of the Factories Act requires first-aid boxes with prescribed contents at the rate of one for every 150 workers ordinarily employed.

q: An applicant under the Right to Information Act, 2005, is unable to make the request for information in writing on account of illiteracy or a sensory disability. In such a case, the Central Public Information Officer is required to:

options.A: Reject the application, as a request can be made only in writing
options.B: Direct the applicant to approach the Central Information Commission
options.C: Ask the applicant to obtain the assistance of a legal practitioner
options.D: Render reasonable assistance to the applicant to reduce the request made orally into writing

e: Section 6 of the RTI Act requires the CPIO to render reasonable assistance to an applicant who cannot write due to illiteracy or sensory disability, to reduce an oral request into writing.

q: A probationer on the Railways completes his period of probation satisfactorily and his case is taken up for confirmation in the post held by him. In regard to such confirmation, the correct position is that:

options.A: He is confirmed automatically in the post from the date of his initial appointment
options.B: Confirmation can be made only against a permanent (substantive) vacancy in the post or grade
options.C: He can be confirmed even if no permanent vacancy exists, by creating a supernumerary post for him
options.D: Confirmation is made in the officiating capacity in which he holds the post

e: Confirmation can be made only against a permanent substantive vacancy in the post or grade; satisfactory probation alone does not create a right to confirmation without such a vacancy.

q: A railway servant avails a spell of leave and a weekly holiday falls immediately before the day he proceeds on leave and another immediately after the day he resumes duty, both being permitted to be prefixed and suffixed to the leave. In regard to those two holidays, the correct position is that:

options.A: The holidays so prefixed and suffixed are not treated as part of the leave
options.B: Both the holidays are debited to the leave account of the railway servant
options.C: Only the holiday suffixed to the leave is treated as part of the leave
options.D: Holidays can never be either prefixed or suffixed to a spell of leave

e: Under the leave rules, holidays permitted to be prefixed or suffixed to leave are not treated as part of the leave and are not debited to the leave account.

q: A railway servant renders a service to a body outside the Government and receives a payment for it from the funds of that body, and not from the general revenues of the Government. Such a payment received by him is classified, under the Establishment rules, as:

options.A: Honorarium
options.B: Fee
options.C: Special pay
options.D: Personal pay

e: A fee is payment received from a non-Government body for service rendered to it, unlike honorarium which is paid from general revenues for Government work.

q: A post is created on the Railways purely to accommodate one particular officer personally. The post does not form part of the regular cadre of any service and it will cease to exist the moment that officer vacates it. Such a post is known as a/an:

options.A: Work-charged post
options.B: Ex-cadre post
options.C: Temporary post
options.D: Supernumerary post

e: A supernumerary post is created purely to accommodate a particular officer personally, is outside the regular cadre and ceases when he vacates it.

q: A railway servant belonging to a particular service is posted against a post which is borne outside the cadre of that service, the post belonging to a different cadre altogether. The post against which he is so posted is called a/an:

options.A: Selection post
options.B: Cadre post
options.C: Ex-cadre post
options.D: Supernumerary post

e: An ex-cadre post is a post borne outside the cadre of the service to which the railway servant belongs, belonging to a different cadre.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Casual leave is not a recognised kind of leave under the Leave Rules and is not debited to the leave account of a railway servant.
2. Casual leave can be combined with any other kind of leave due to a railway servant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Casual leave is not a recognised kind of leave and is not debited to the leave account, and it cannot be combined with any other kind of leave, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A railway servant is transferred to another station purely at his own request and he applies for joining time to take up his duties at the new station. In regard to his claim for joining time, the correct position is that:

options.A: Joining time is admissible to him as in a transfer in public interest
options.B: Joining time is not admissible to him, the transfer being at his own request
options.C: Joining time is admissible to him at half the normal rates
options.D: Joining time is admissible only if he is a gazetted officer

e: Joining time is admissible only on transfer in public interest. On transfer at own request, no joining time is admissible under the rules.

q: A railway servant is granted commuted leave on medical certificate for a spell. The leave salary admissible to him for that spell of commuted leave is:

options.A: Half of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.B: Nil, as no leave salary is payable during commuted leave
options.C: The same as the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: 75 per cent of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay

e: Commuted leave is granted by converting Leave on Half Average Pay, but leave salary during commuted leave is the same as during Leave on Average Pay.

q: A railway servant completes an approved course of study for which study leave was granted to him, and on his return his leave account is examined. In regard to the debit of that study leave, the correct position is that the study leave is:

options.A: Debited against his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: Debited against his Leave on Half Average Pay account
options.C: Treated as dies non for the period of the course
options.D: Not debited to his leave account

e: Study leave is a separate kind of leave and is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay or Leave on Half Average Pay account of the railway servant.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 22 years of qualifying service, that is, 44 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at retirement are Rs 64,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period: Rs 64,000 divided by 4 is Rs 16,000, multiplied by 44 gives Rs 7,04,000.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 48,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 24,000 per month. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his pension account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: Government NPS contribution is 14 percent of basic pay plus DA: 14 percent of Rs 72,000 (Rs 48,000 plus Rs 24,000) is Rs 10,080.

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 58,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate of 30 per cent of the last pay drawn will be:

options.A: Rs 29,000 per month
options.B: Rs 23,200 per month
options.C: Rs 17,400 per month
options.D: Rs 11,600 per month

e: Normal family pension is 30 percent of last pay drawn: 30 percent of Rs 58,000 is Rs 17,400 per month.

q: A railway pensioner drawing a basic pension of Rs 35,000 per month attains the age of 80 years. The total pension admissible to him thereafter, including the additional quantum of pension at 20 per cent of the basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 38,500 per month
options.B: Rs 45,500 per month
options.C: Rs 52,500 per month
options.D: Rs 42,000 per month

e: At age 80, additional pension is 20 percent of basic pension: Rs 35,000 plus Rs 7,000 is Rs 42,000 per month.

q: A question arises in a railway office as to the manner in which reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes is to be applied in a direct recruitment. The correct position is that the reservation is operated through:

options.A: Vacancy-based rosters, applied only to the vacancies arising in a year
options.B: Post-based rosters, the roster points being applied to the posts in a cadre
options.C: Seniority lists maintained separately for each reserved category
options.D: Waiting lists prepared by the Railway Recruitment Board

e: After the Supreme Court ruling, reservation in direct recruitment is operated through post-based rosters applied to posts in the cadre, not vacancy-based rosters.

q: Two direct recruits appointed to a grade in the same selection are bracketed at the same position in the order of merit assigned by the selecting authority. Their inter-se seniority in the grade is decided by:

options.A: Date of birth, the older candidate ranking senior
options.B: The length of service rendered by each in any previous post
options.C: The higher educational qualification possessed by each
options.D: The earlier date of submission of application by each

e: When direct recruits are bracketed at the same merit position, inter-se seniority is decided by date of birth, the older candidate ranking senior.

q: A railway servant had rendered a spell of service on an ad hoc, fortuitous basis in a grade before he was regularly appointed to that grade. In regard to counting of that ad hoc spell towards his seniority in the grade, the correct position is that such ad hoc service:

options.A: Counts in full towards seniority in that grade
options.B: Counts to the extent of one-half towards seniority
options.C: Does not count towards seniority in that grade
options.D: Counts towards seniority only if it exceeds one year

e: Ad hoc or fortuitous service rendered before regular appointment does not count towards seniority in that grade under the seniority rules.

q: A railway servant in the Aye medical category, whose duties are connected with train working, is 40 years of age. The interval at which he is required to undergo Periodical Medical Examination at that age is:

options.A: Every year
options.B: Every two years
options.C: Every three years
options.D: Every four years

e: For Aye category staff connected with train working, Periodical Medical Examination up to age 45 is at an interval of every four years, so at age 40 it is four-yearly.

q: In the medical classification prescribed for railway servants, the category denoted as Aye-One (A-1) stands for:

options.A: The highest medical fitness category, prescribed for staff whose duties are directly connected with the running of trains and require the strictest standards of physical fitness and vision
options.B: The category prescribing the lowest standard of vision
options.C: The category applicable only to ministerial staff working in offices
options.D: A category which has since been abolished on the Railways

e: Aye-One (A-1) is the highest medical fitness category, prescribed for staff directly connected with running of trains requiring the strictest fitness and vision standards.

q: A railway servant who is blind is posted at a station and claims Transport Allowance for commuting between his residence and his office. The rate at which Transport Allowance is admissible to him is:

options.A: The normal rate admissible to other railway servants
options.B: Double the normal rate of Transport Allowance
options.C: One and a half times the normal rate
options.D: Half of the normal rate

e: Blind railway servants are admissible Transport Allowance at double the normal rate, to meet the higher cost of commuting.

q: A railway servant is provided with a staff car for commuting between his residence and his office, the facility being available to him regularly. In regard to his claim for Transport Allowance, the correct position is that Transport Allowance is:

options.A: Admissible to him at the full normal rate
options.B: Admissible to him at half of the normal rate
options.C: Not admissible to him, as he is provided with official transport for commuting
options.D: Admissible only on the days on which the staff car is not used

e: Transport Allowance is not admissible to a railway servant provided with official transport or a staff car for commuting between residence and office.

q: A woman railway servant with a disability claims the Special Allowance for Child Care admissible to such employees. The allowance is payable to her:

options.A: In respect of all her children till they attain the age of 18 years
options.B: In respect of only one child, till the child attains the age of one year
options.C: In respect of her two eldest surviving children till they attain the age of five years
options.D: In respect of her two eldest surviving children, from their birth till they attain the age of two years

e: Special Allowance for Child Care for women with disabilities is payable for the two eldest surviving children from birth till they attain the age of two years.

q: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the Risk and Hardship Matrix introduced for railway servants is meant to:

options.A: Grade the various risk and hardship allowances into cells according to the level of risk and hardship involved in the duties
options.B: Classify cities for the purpose of House Rent Allowance
options.C: Determine the rate of Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants
options.D: Fix the rates of Transport Allowance for different cities

e: The 7th CPC Risk and Hardship Matrix grades risk and hardship allowances into cells according to the level of risk and hardship involved in the duties.

q: A railway servant could not avail the Leave Travel Concession due to him for a particular block during the block period itself. He may still avail that concession:

options.A: At any time during the next two blocks
options.B: In the first year of the succeeding block, as a grace period
options.C: Only at the time of his retirement
options.D: In no case, as it lapses absolutely at the end of the block

e: LTC not availed in its block can be availed in the first year of the succeeding block as a grace period, under the LTC carry-forward rule.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Home Town Leave Travel Concession is admissible to a railway servant once in a block of two years.
2. Anywhere in India Leave Travel Concession is admissible once in a block of four years, in lieu of one Home Town Leave Travel Concession entitlement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Home Town LTC is admissible once in a block of two years, and All India LTC once in a block of four years in lieu of one Home Town LTC, so both statements are correct.

q: The unmarried daughter of a deceased railway servant is in receipt of family pension and she attains the age of 25 years, remaining unmarried and not earning her livelihood. In regard to continuance of her family pension beyond that age, the correct position is that:

options.A: It stops automatically on her attaining the age of 25 years
options.B: It continues only up to the age of 30 years in all cases
options.C: It continues only if she was below 25 years of age at the time of the death of the railway servant
options.D: It continues even beyond the age of 25 years, until she gets married or remarried, or starts earning her livelihood

e: Family pension to an unmarried daughter continues beyond age 25 until she marries or remarries or starts earning her livelihood, whichever is earliest.

q: The son of a deceased railway servant suffers from a disability of mind and is physically unable to earn his livelihood, as certified by the competent medical authority. The family pension admissible in his case is payable:

options.A: For his lifetime, even beyond the age of 25 years
options.B: Only up to the age of 25 years
options.C: Only up to the age of 21 years
options.D: Only up to the age of 18 years

e: A son suffering from disability of mind or unable to earn livelihood, duly certified, is eligible for family pension for his lifetime beyond age 25.

q: A son of a deceased railway servant is otherwise eligible for family pension. The family pension ordinarily remains payable to him until he:

options.A: Attains the age of 18 years
options.B: Attains the age of 25 years, gets married, or starts earning his livelihood, whichever is the earliest
options.C: Attains the age of 21 years, whether or not he is earning
options.D: Attains the age of 30 years in all cases

e: Family pension to a son is ordinarily payable until he attains age 25, gets married, or starts earning his livelihood, whichever is earliest.

q: A railway servant is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking, with the permission of the competent authority, on rendering service under the Railways. The pensionary benefit sanctioned to him for the qualifying service rendered by him under the Railways, proportionate to that service, is known as:

options.A: Invalid pension
options.B: Compensation pension
options.C: Pro-rata pension
options.D: Extraordinary pension

e: On permanent absorption in a PSU, pension proportionate to qualifying service rendered under Government is termed pro-rata pension.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund applies for a final, non-refundable withdrawal from the Fund to meet the expenditure of a pleasure trip abroad for himself and his family. In regard to his application, the correct position is that such a withdrawal:

options.A: Is permissible up to 75 per cent of the balance at his credit
options.B: Is permissible up to 50 per cent of the balance at his credit
options.C: Is permissible only after he completes 25 years of service
options.D: Is not a permissible purpose for a final withdrawal from the Fund

e: Final withdrawal from GPF is permitted only for specified purposes like marriage, education and medical treatment; a pleasure trip abroad is not a permissible purpose.

q: The nominee of a member of the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme claims the benefit under the scheme on the death of the member while in service. In regard to that benefit, the correct position is that:

options.A: The member was required to pay a monthly premium for the insurance cover
options.B: An assurance benefit, linked to the balance in the member's Provident Fund account, is payable to the nominee, without any contribution by the employee
options.C: A fixed sum of Rs 10,000 is payable in all cases
options.D: The scheme covers the medical expenses of the family of the member

e: Under EDLI, an assurance benefit linked to the Provident Fund balance is payable on death in service without any contribution by the employee.

q: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the monthly subscription paid by a member is apportioned between the Insurance Fund and the Savings Fund in the proportion of:

options.A: 30 per cent to the Insurance Fund and 70 per cent to the Savings Fund
options.B: 50 per cent to the Insurance Fund and 50 per cent to the Savings Fund
options.C: 70 per cent to the Insurance Fund and 30 per cent to the Savings Fund
options.D: 25 per cent to the Insurance Fund and 75 per cent to the Savings Fund

e: Under CGEGIS, the monthly subscription is apportioned 30 percent to the Insurance Fund and 70 percent to the Savings Fund.

q: On the implementation of the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission, the pay of a serving railway servant in the pre-revised structure was fixed in the revised pay matrix by multiplying his pre-revised pay by a fitment factor of:
e: On 7th CPC implementation, pay was fixed by multiplying pre-revised pay by the fitment factor of 2.57 and placing it in the pay matrix.

q: A candidate is appointed by direct recruitment to an entry-level post placed in Level 1 of the pay matrix introduced under the 7th CPC. The minimum pay prescribed at that level, at which his pay will ordinarily be fixed on appointment, is:

options.A: Rs 15,700 per month
options.B: Rs 19,900 per month
options.C: Rs 21,700 per month
options.D: Rs 18,000 per month

e: Level 1 of the 7th CPC pay matrix starts at Rs 18,000 per month, at which pay of a direct recruit to an entry-level post is ordinarily fixed.

q: For the purpose of House Rent Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation, a city is classified as X class, attracting the highest rate of the allowance, if its population is:

options.A: 50 lakh and above
options.B: 25 lakh and above
options.C: 10 lakh and above
options.D: 1 crore and above

e: For HRA under the 7th CPC, X class cities are those with population of 50 lakh and above, attracting the highest rate.

q: Dearness Allowance admissible to railway servants crosses 50 per cent of basic pay. On such crossing, the rates of House Rent Allowance in X, Y and Z class cities respectively stand revised to:

options.A: 24 per cent, 16 per cent and 8 per cent of basic pay
options.B: 30 per cent, 20 per cent and 10 per cent of basic pay
options.C: 27 per cent, 18 per cent and 9 per cent of basic pay
options.D: 32 per cent, 22 per cent and 12 per cent of basic pay

e: When DA crosses 50 percent, HRA rates are revised to 30 percent, 20 percent and 10 percent of basic pay for X, Y and Z class cities respectively.

q: For the computation of Night Duty Allowance, the night duty performed by a railway servant between 22:00 hours and 06:00 hours is given a weightage of:

options.A: 5 minutes for every hour of night duty
options.B: 20 minutes for every hour of night duty
options.C: 10 minutes for every hour of night duty
options.D: 30 minutes for every hour of night duty

e: For Night Duty Allowance, night duty between 22:00 and 06:00 hours carries a weightage of 10 minutes for every hour of night duty.

q: Staff classified as Continuous under the Hours of Employment Regulations are rostered for 48 hours of work in a week. The period of rest to which such staff are entitled in a week is not less than:

options.A: 24 consecutive hours
options.B: 36 consecutive hours, without any condition about the night
options.C: 30 consecutive hours, without any condition about the night
options.D: 30 consecutive hours including one full night

e: Staff classified as Continuous under HOER, rostered for 48 hours a week, are entitled to weekly rest of not less than 30 consecutive hours including one full night.

q: A railway servant sustains a disablement which is established to be attributable to the conditions of his service, the injury having been sustained by him in the course of his duty. The pension admissible to him on that account is:

options.A: Extraordinary pension, including disability pension
options.B: Invalid pension
options.C: Compensation pension
options.D: Superannuation pension

e: Pension for disablement attributable to service conditions and sustained in the course of duty is extraordinary pension, including disability pension.

q: A railway servant is detained on duty beyond his rostered hours of work and overtime allowance becomes payable to him for those hours. Such overtime allowance is ordinarily payable at:

options.A: The ordinary rate of pay
options.B: Twice, that is double, the ordinary rate of pay
options.C: One and a half times the ordinary rate of pay
options.D: Two and a half times the ordinary rate of pay

e: Overtime allowance for duty beyond rostered hours under HOER is ordinarily payable at twice, that is double, the ordinary rate of pay.

q: A railway servant draws emoluments of Rs 38,000 per month. The minimum amount of subscription payable by him to the General Provident Fund, at 6 per cent of his emoluments, will be:

options.A: Rs 3,800 per month
options.B: Rs 3,040 per month
options.C: Rs 2,280 per month
options.D: Rs 4,560 per month

e: Minimum GPF subscription is 6 percent of emoluments: 6 percent of Rs 38,000 is Rs 2,280 per month.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for 9 hours on a day, the absence being for more than 6 hours but less than 12 hours. The admissible rate of Daily Allowance for the station is Rs 1,200 per day. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day, at 70 per cent of the admissible rate, will be:

options.A: Rs 360
options.B: Rs 600
options.D: Rs 840

e: For absence of more than 6 hours but less than 12 hours, Daily Allowance is 70 percent of the rate: 70 percent of Rs 1,200 is Rs 840.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 30,000 per month applies for a House Building Advance. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him, at 139 times his basic pay and being within the overall ceiling of Rs 1 crore, will be:
e: House Building Advance is 139 times basic pay subject to the Rs 1 crore ceiling: 139 multiplied by Rs 30,000 is Rs 41,70,000, within the ceiling.

q: A break, that is an interruption, occurs in the service of a railway servant and the break is not condoned by the competent authority. The effect of that interruption on his past service, for the purpose of pension, is that:

options.A: Half of his past service is forfeited for pension
options.B: His past service is forfeited for pension, the break not having been condoned
options.C: Only the date of his next increment is postponed
options.D: There is no consequence for the purpose of pension

e: An interruption in service not condoned by the competent authority entails forfeiture of past service for pension purposes.

q: A person joins railway service at a young age and a question arises as to the date from which his service will begin to count as qualifying service for pension. Qualifying service for pension commences from the date on which he attains the age of:

options.A: 16 years
options.B: 21 years
options.C: 18 years
options.D: 25 years

e: Qualifying service for pension commences from the date a railway servant attains the age of 18 years.

q: A railway servant dies while in service and family pension at the enhanced rate becomes payable to his family. In such a case, the enhanced rate remains payable for a period of:

options.A: 5 years, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.B: 10 years in all cases, irrespective of age
options.C: 7 years, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.D: 7 years, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 67 years, whichever is earlier

e: Enhanced family pension on death in service is payable for 7 years or till the deceased would have attained age 67 years, whichever is earlier.

q: As a result of work studies, a railway unit surrenders a number of posts which are no longer required in that unit. The posts so surrendered are dealt with in the manner that they are:

options.A: Treated as lapsed permanently and can never be revived
options.B: Transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Utilised only for works expenditure of the Railway
options.D: Credited to the Vacancy Bank, from which they can be utilised for creation of posts or for redeployment purposes

e: Posts surrendered after work studies are credited to the Vacancy Bank, from which they can be used for creation of posts or redeployment.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding quarantine leave admissible to a railway servant on account of an infectious disease in his family or household:
1. Quarantine leave is not debited to the leave account of the railway servant.
2. Quarantine leave is ordinarily granted for a period not exceeding 21 days at a time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Quarantine leave for infectious disease in the family is not debited to the leave account and is ordinarily granted up to 21 days at a time, so both statements are correct.

q: A railway servant applies for leave preparatory to retirement and requests that the leave be allowed to run for two months beyond the date on which he is due to retire from service. The correct position is that leave preparatory to retirement:

options.A: May extend up to six months beyond the date of retirement
options.B: Cannot extend beyond the date on which he is due to retire from service
options.C: Is admissible only in the form of Leave on Half Average Pay
options.D: Is debited to the leave account of the succeeding year

e: Leave preparatory to retirement cannot extend beyond the date on which the railway servant is due to retire from service.

q: A railway servant remains absent from duty without any authorisation for a continuous period exceeding five years and does not respond to any communication from his office. Under the leave rules, the position in his case is that he is:

options.A: Deemed to have resigned from railway service, unless the competent authority, in view of the circumstances of the case, determines otherwise
options.B: Granted Extra Ordinary Leave for the entire period automatically
options.C: Treated as having retired voluntarily from service
options.D: Placed under suspension for the entire period of his absence

e: Unauthorised absence exceeding five years continuously makes the railway servant deemed to have resigned, unless the competent authority determines otherwise.

q: A railway servant is granted Work Related Illness and Injury Leave (WRIIL) for an illness directly attributable to the discharge of his official duty. The leave salary admissible to him is:

options.A: Full pay and allowances during the entire period of hospitalisation; beyond hospitalisation, full pay and allowances for the six months immediately following hospitalisation and half pay for twelve months beyond that period
options.B: Equal to the leave salary during Leave on Average Pay for the first 120 days and equal to the leave salary during Leave on Half Average Pay thereafter, without limit
options.C: Equal to the leave salary during Leave on Half Average Pay for the entire period
options.D: Nil, as WRIIL carries no leave salary

e: Under WRIIL, full pay and allowances are admissible during hospitalisation, then full pay for six months after hospitalisation and half pay for twelve months beyond that.

q: A railway servant has reached the maximum of his pay level and is awaiting a stagnation increment. He becomes eligible for a stagnation increment after every:

options.A: One year
options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: Five years

e: A railway servant at the maximum of his pay level becomes eligible for a stagnation increment after every two years.
